vocabulary.headword: get on like a house on fire

content.v: Gloria Bruce and Shirley Clements shouldn’t have been penfriends.

Their friendship resulted from a happy accident in 1953. Both of them were then in elementary school. Bruce was in New Orleans, Louisiana, and Clements was in Batley, England. One of Bruce’s classmates had a British penfriend, and some of that girl’s friends wanted penfriends of their own. Bruce wrote to a girl named Susan. However, when she got a letter back, it was from Clements.
No matter—Bruce and Clements had a lot in common. Both loved reading and collecting stamps. Both had learnt to
from their mothers. Their birthdays were ten days apart. And as they grew older, their similarities only deepened.
The women’s means of connection changed with time. At first, they wrote long letters. They weighed the envelopes at the post office before sending them across the ocean. To
Christmas gifts, they had to mail the packages in November. They watched the clock during their first phone call, because a few minutes would cost $35.
The two finally met in person in 1985. Clements, then a
, stopped in New Orleans after a meeting in California. As soon as they met, their worries about whether they would like each other in person were
. Clements did a crawfish boil with Bruce and her family. “We
got on like a house on fire
from the first minute until now,” Clements said.

After that first visit, the friends saw each other whenever they could. Clements stopped in Louisiana after other business trips. Bruce flew to Clements’s home three times. They even went on five sea trips around the world. And, of course, they continued to write to each other. They have now exchanged 700 letters.

”. Bruce says the secret to their lasting friendship is laughter. “She’s fun,” she said. “What can I say?”

prompt.v: Gloria Bruce and Shirley Clements still write to each other now, don’t they?
Why did the author write that Bruce and Clements shouldn’t have been penfriends in Paragraph 1?
Why did Bruce and Clements watch the clock during their first phone call?
Bruce thinks the secret to her lasting friendship with Clements is laughter. From your point of view, what is the secret to lasting friendships? Why?
